The first reading's notes (a) and (b), that the labels are not on the device, are not lettering defects. These two labels are product callouts, not text on a screen. Neither is placed on a device, and neither covers one. In 02-3 Meera is the only person, holding the phone directly above the label. Notes (c) and (d), about the time cue and Meera's entrance, concern art and source; the caption marks onboarding and the sunset window marks the time. Note (e), about hair, is art continuity.
Natural scan: 02-1 caption at top-left, then the top-right label; 02-2 balloon; 02-3 top balloon, then the lower label; 02-4 balloon. This is the script order.
No two balloons from different speakers sit close enough to be misread. The question-free statements read Ananya, Meera ('And our team...' follows on from Ananya's line), then Ananya.

Same evening office, with the open laptop on the desk behind Meera. Her 'And our team...' continues Ananya's workflow line.
Two-shot in the same room. Meera holds the same phone at her side, and Ananya's line closes the exchange.

The evening office cuts to the bright, tidy reception. The 03-1 caption 'A later morning: patients can always check in at the front desk.' marks the time and place change at the new page boundary. Meera, now at the desk, carries over.

The time and entrance notes concern art and source and are carried by the caption and lighting. At the new 02-4→03-1 boundary, the 'A later morning' caption resolves the time jump. Nothing unresolved remains.
